bbs-daily-rep-summary: Daily summary of one California state book rep's working day for Parker, from the rep's own end-of-day check-in plus the systems of record, so Parker can see the work, spot where to help, and hold the rep to their own commitments, without surveillance. Two modes: check-in (the rep, end of day: draft their own five-minute report, including off-computer work such as calls, visits, sizings and portals) and summary (Parker, next morning, usually a scheduled Routine: reads the check-in from Teams, pipeline from the Sales CRM, bookings from Business Central, quote-folder activity from SharePoint; writes one file to Parker's folder, sends nothing). Use when Parker says "daily summary for <rep>", "what did <rep> do yesterday" or "set up the daily rep routine", or a rep says "draft my check-in" or "what do I tell Parker". Do NOT use for a week or longer (bbs-weekly-sales-report), to read any mailbox but the signed-in person's, or to rate a rep from timestamps.
bbs-quote-builder: Render a Claude-built PDF copy of a Black Box Safety, Inc. (BBS) sales quote that already exists in Business Central, in the BC print layout and numbered with that quote's SQ number. Since 2026-10-16 this is a fallback, not the quote desk's path: the customer quote is created in Business Central (items through bc-item-entry, header and lines through bc-quote-entry; /ca-rfq Gate 5) and the customer document is the PDF BC prints from the released quote. Use this skill only when a rep asks for a Claude-rendered copy of an existing BC quote ("render SQ-###### as a PDF", "put SQ-###### on our letterhead", "I can't print from BC, build the PDF") or for a side-by-side proof against the BC print. Do NOT use it to create or edit quote records in Business Central, to price anything, or for vendor sourcing emails (use bbs-sourcing).
bbs-sourcing: Source pricing from vendors for a competitive bid RFQ at Black Box Safety. Use this skill whenever a BBS sales rep needs to turn an inbound competitive RFQ from a California state agency into vendor outreach — including when they say "source this RFQ," "get me pricing on these items," "reach out to vendors for this bid," "help me quote this," or paste/upload an RFQ worksheet and ask what to do next. Also use when the rep wants to follow up with non-responding vendors or leverage one vendor's quote against another's. Always use this skill for competitive, SB/DVBE, or Fair-and-Reasonable bids. DO NOT use when the RFQ is NASPO-routed or every item is available on grainger.com — those go through Provision Connect instead. Output is a sourcing brief plus vendor emails drafted in BBS's voice, rendered inline with pop-out buttons for Outlook.
bbs-weekly-sales-report: Build Parker Marshall's weekly sales summary of his own, Kim Quezon's and Aanya Samarasinghe's week on the California state agency book, written to ~/weekly-sales-reports/YYYY-MM-DD_weekly-sales-report.md under that week's Monday. Use when Parker says "weekly sales report", "write up the week", "what did the team do this week", "I have to fill out the sales form", "pull the numbers for the weekly", or asks for quotes, RFQs, orders or bookings over a named week or "last week". Use it too for a per-rep question over a week — "how did Aanya do this week", "what did Kim quote", "did we submit everything that was due" — because Business Central's salesperson codes cannot split Aanya out of a shared bucket and its quote records miss most of the pipeline; the Sales CRM is the pipeline. Do NOT use for a month, quarter or fiscal-year-to-date figure; those are booked-revenue questions for Business Central directly.
bc-item-entry: Enter new product items into Business Central (BC) for Black Box Safety, each with a vendor and a cost, after the rep has reviewed exactly what will be written. Use this skill whenever a BBS rep needs item cards created in BC: "add these items to BC", "enter these products", "set up the item cards for this PO", "these SKUs aren't in Business Central yet", "create the items so I can build the quote", or any time a quote or sales order needs an item number that BC does not have. Also use it when a rep hands over a vendor quote, price list, or Grainger pricing and wants the products on file. Always use this skill for item creation so every card carries a vendor, a sourced cost, the house posting groups, and a named approval. Do NOT use it to edit existing items, to create vendors (the rep does that in BC), to build the sales quote (bc-quote-entry does that, after the items exist), or to load the website catalog (bbs-pricelist-import).
bc-quote-entry: Create the customer's sales quote in Business Central (BC) for Black Box Safety: the header and lines, from a spec the rep has reviewed and approved by name, under the rep's own sign-in. Use this skill whenever a BBS rep has priced an RFQ and wants the quote in BC: "create the quote in BC", "build the sales quote for this RFQ", "put these lines on a BC quote for Cal Fire", "enter the quote so I can release it", "make the SQ", or when /ca-rfq or naspo-quote reaches the build-the-quote step. Every line's item must already exist in BC; a missing item stops and is entered through bc-item-entry first. The quote number is the one BC assigns, read back. Do NOT use it to create or edit items (bc-item-entry), to release, convert, send or print the quote (a person does that in BC), to render a PDF copy of an existing BC quote (bbs-quote-builder), or for sales orders, invoices or purchase orders.
ca-agency-primer: Build the background briefing that lets a rep understand a California state agency as a system rather than one facility — what the department does, how its sites differ, where the money is, and where Black Box Safety stands at each location. Use when a rep is taking on an agency or preparing for a first meeting inside a multi-site department, or asks what an agency is, what its facilities do, how many sites it has, why one site buys differently from another, or where the whitespace is across CDCR, DSH, CalVet, Caltrans, Cal Fire, CHP or DGS. Use it too for narrower asks — "tell me about Patton", "why is this agency so small for us", "which facility should we be at" — because a single-site answer inside a multi-site department usually hides the real finding. Keeps public agency facts, internal BC and CRM figures and SCPRS slices visibly separate, and says "data pending" where BBS has no history. Not for one booked meeting (ca-site-visit-brief).
ca-budget-timing: Translate the California budget and procurement calendar into sales timing — when an agency has money, when it must encumber it, and which deadline governs a specific deal. Use whenever anyone asks when to call an agency, whether money lapses on 30 June, what an encumbrance deadline is, whether a deal can still land this fiscal year, when the DGS cutoff falls, what the enacted budget gave an agency such as CHP, CAL FIRE, State Hospitals or Caltrans, whether an augmentation is one-time or ongoing, or how to sequence a quarter's selling. Use it before promising a buyer any date: 30 June does not govern everything (deals above delegated authority go through DGS around 1 April), California's fiscal year does not govern federally funded items, and a lapsing appropriation needs a signed PO by the deadline, not a delivery. Not for an RFQ's own due date, which belongs to that request's run record.
ca-form-filler: Fill any California state compliance form or bid packet for Black Box Safety — the CDCR OBS 4007(B) "Packet B", and standalone forms including STD 204, STD 205, DGS PD 843, GSPD-05-105 Bidder Declaration, DGS PD 1 and OBS 1500 Darfur, OBS 1000 GenAI, CalRecycle 74 and CV 012. Use whenever a rep uploads blank state forms or a bid packet, mentions any of those form numbers, or says "Packet B", "OBS 4007", "the CDCR forms", "the bid packet", "state forms", "compliance forms", or "fill out the forms". It merges BBS's canonical vendor profile with the solicitation, fills every field it can verify, signs BBS's own lines and flags any signer it cannot determine, and reports what it could not fill. Do NOT use to price items (grainger-pricing), build the customer quote (bbs-quote-builder), extract line items from a cart PDF or screenshot (rfq-item-extract), or run a whole NASPO response end to end (naspo-quote, which calls this for the paperwork).
ca-rfq-intake: Log an inbound California state quote request into the right customer folder and open its run record — the first move on any state RFQ, NASPO or competitive. Use this the moment a request arrives from a CDCR institution, CalVet home, DSH hospital, Caltrans district, CalFire unit, CMD, DWR, or any State of California agency, whether it comes as an email with attachments, a bare item list, a Line-Item Cost Worksheet, or a portal link — and use it before pricing anything, because an RFQ that never got logged is the one that misses its deadline. Also use it when asked to file, log, intake, or "start" a state quote request, or to find where a request should live.
ca-site-visit-brief: Build the document set a rep walks into a California state agency site visit with — a long-form call plan for the night before and a one-screen pocket card for the parking lot. Use whenever a rep has a meeting, site visit, first call, QBR, check-in or introduction booked at any CA state facility, or someone asks to prep for a call, brief a rep, build talking points, or work out what to say at CDCR, DSH, CalVet, Caltrans, CHP, Cal Fire or any agency site. Use it too for narrower asks — "what should Aanya lead with at Metro", "what do we know about this buyer", "why did this site go quiet", "what do I ask them" — because a pile of account facts is not a call plan. Produces the facts, the order to say them in, the questions, and the explicit list of numbers not to say aloud, keeping what BC and the CRM prove apart from public documents, inference and the unknown. Not for agency-wide background (ca-agency-primer).
ca-territory-handoff: Segment a California state agency book by relationship state and turn it into a dated, prioritized call list a rep can work on Monday. Use when a rep takes over accounts, a departed rep's book needs re-homing, or someone asks which accounts have gone quiet, who Kim or Aanya should call first, how to split CDCR, Caltrans or any agency between reps, or for a handover, territory launch, account blitz or win-back plan. Use it too for analysis-only asks — "which accounts are at risk", "where is our whitespace at CMD", "size the winnable pond at CalVet", "which facilities have a Grainger account but never ordered" — because a segmentation without dated actions is a spreadsheet nobody works. Bands the book into recover, defend, watch, provisioned whitespace and cold start, each with its own opening words. Do NOT use to log or price a request or worksheet that has arrived (that is /ca-rfq), or to write outreach sequences.
ca-visit-readiness-review: Pressure-test a finished California state agency call plan, account brief or leave-behind before a rep walks in with it, from the point of view of the person who has to say it in the room. Use whenever a visit brief, call plan, pocket card, talking points or customer-facing leave-behind has been drafted and someone asks to review it, sanity-check it, or get a second opinion — and when the brief is finished and nobody asked, because an unreviewed prep document is the one that puts an inferred job title or a slice-limited market figure in front of a procurement officer. It checks five things — what a rep would add, what would hurt them in the room, whether the product story is right, which catalog gaps need verifying, and whether it works on a phone ten minutes before the meeting. Do NOT use to write the brief itself (ca-site-visit-brief) or for agency background (ca-agency-primer).
dgs-bpo-item-check: Determine whether Grainger part numbers are on California's DGS Blanket Purchase Order item list by looking each one up in the bundled BPO master list, which names its fiscal year and warns when that year has ended. Use whenever a rep asks to check, verify, confirm, or cross-reference Grainger part numbers against the BPO, the DGS blanket purchase order, or the BPO list — "is this on the BPO", "BPO check", "are these approved". Answers on-list or off-list from the bundled file only; never from memory and never a guess. Do NOT use to obtain a price (use grainger-pricing) or to extract item numbers from a PDF, cart or screenshot. If a rep says only "check these Grainger items" without making clear whether they mean BPO eligibility or price, ask which before running.
grainger-pricing: Get live Grainger pricing, stock and ship dates for Black Box Safety through the Grainger MCP — the authorized path for every Grainger price at BBS, which replaced the b2b.blackboxsafety.com punch-out. Use whenever a rep wants unit prices for Grainger item numbers, is filling the Unit Price column of an RFQ or NASPO worksheet, asks what Grainger charges on a facility's account, needs an item number found from a description or manufacturer part number, asks which account a buyer prices on, or asks whether something is in stock and when it ships. Never price a Grainger item from the open web or from memory. Do NOT use to extract item numbers from a cart PDF, screenshot or DWR RFQ (rfq-item-extract produces the list this prices), to check DGS BPO eligibility (dgs-bpo-item-check), or to build the quote document (bbs-quote-builder). If a rep says only "check these items", ask whether they mean price or BPO eligibility.
grainger-promo-page: Build a Black Box Safety product promotion landing page for a California public agency from a Grainger negotiated hot list or price sheet, with live pricing, product photography, a quote builder, SCPRS-sized buyer segments, and the brand compliance gate. Use this skill whenever a Grainger rep sends a priced sheet or hot list for an agency, whenever someone asks for a promo page, contract sheet, product landing page, punchout promo, or campaign page for CAL FIRE, CDCR, DWR, CHP, Caltrans, CalVet, a CSU or UC campus, or any other California agency, and whenever someone says they want to promote Grainger items or a hot list to an agency by email or web. Also use it when asked to price a list of Grainger item numbers for an agency account, or to segment an agency's buyers for a campaign.
naspo-quote: Run a complete California state agency RFQ response end to end and deliver both halves: live Grainger pricing for the requested item numbers, the BBS sales quote PDF, and the filled CA compliance packet (OBS Line-Item Cost Worksheet, CalRecycle 74, DGS PD 843, Darfur OBS 1500, OBS 1000 GenAI, Bidder Declaration GSPD-05-105). Use whenever a CDCR institution, CalVet home, CSU/UC campus, Caltrans district or any State of California agency asks for pricing on item numbers, sends blank state certs to complete, or both — even if they never say NASPO, and even when the ask looks like only pricing or only paperwork, because on state business the two halves ship together. An agency email that asks for a quote is this skill, not an intake task: ca-rfq-intake only files a request and opens its folder, and does not price or fill anything. Do NOT use for a competitive SB/DVBE bid needing vendor sourcing (use bbs-sourcing), or when the rep wants the forms alone with no pricing (use ca-form-filler).
rfq-item-extract: Pull item numbers and quantities out of whatever a customer or agency sent, and return them in the format the next step needs. Three sources: a Grainger cart saved or printed as a PDF; a screenshot or image (PNG, JPG) of a Grainger cart, order or item table; and a California Department of Water Resources Request for Quotation PDF — spoken of as DWR, a DWR RFQ, or "the DWR PDF" — including scanned and image-only files. Use whenever a rep wants the items pulled out of a file or an image: "get the item numbers and quantities", "pull the items from this cart", "extract from this screenshot", "DWR PDF info". Output is ITEM#,QTY lines ready to paste into the Grainger purchasing portal, or the DWR sourcing table. Do NOT use to price items (grainger-pricing), to check DGS BPO eligibility (dgs-bpo-item-check), or to fill state forms (ca-form-filler) — this produces the list those consume. If a rep says only "check these items", ask whether they mean price or BPO eligibility.
sam-gov-opportunities: Look up open federal solicitations on SAM.gov by NAICS code, agency, solicitation number or title words, through the official Get Opportunities API, and say for each one whether BBS can respond to its set-aside as an SDVOSB, VOSB and federal small business. Read-only: one GET request per NAICS code, BBS's shared key from the SAM_GOV_API_KEY environment variable. Use when Kim, Griffin or any rep asks "what's open on SAM for NAICS …", "any SDVOSB set-asides at the VA", "is this solicitation still open", "federal opportunities in California", or wants the current list of open federal notices before a pursuit or a deck. Do NOT use for past federal awards, incumbents or spend (usaspending-awards), California state bids (ca-rfq-intake, SCPRS), drafting a response or a deck (bbs-deck-voice), or registering, bidding or submitting anything on SAM.gov — this skill only reads.
usaspending-awards: Look up past federal contract awards on USAspending.gov: who won contracts under a NAICS code or at an agency, how much, and when; who the biggest vendors are in a federal market; which primes a company has been a reported first-tier subcontractor under; and BBS's own federal award history by its UEI. Read-only search of the public USAspending API, no key. Use when Kim, Griffin or any rep asks "who won the last VA award for NAICS …", "who's the incumbent", "what has DoD bought under 339113", "top vendors for body armor at DHS", "what federal awards has BBS won", or "which primes has this company subcontracted under". Do NOT use for open solicitations that can still be bid (sam-gov-opportunities), California state purchasing (SCPRS, ca-procurement-intel), BBS's own books (Business Central), or drafting a pursuit or deck (bbs-deck-voice). It only reads.
vendor-quote-email: Generates a vendor pricing quote request email for a Black Box Safety, Inc. sales rep. Use this skill whenever the user asks to draft a vendor quote email, pricing request, or wants to email a vendor/supplier for pricing. Trigger phrases include: "draft a quote email", "vendor quote", "pricing request email", "email a vendor for pricing", "quote request", "create a quote email", or any request to contact a vendor/supplier for item pricing on behalf of a customer agency. Always render the interactive form widget — never draft this email as free-form text without showing the form first.
bbs-deck-voice: Generate customer-facing PowerPoint slide copy in Parker Marshall's voice for Black Box Safety (BBS) federal pursuits (SDVOSB / GSA Schedule / set-asides). Use this skill whenever Parker needs slide headlines, sub-bullets, speaker notes, or full-deck copy for a federal customer or teaming presentation, or says "write the deck copy," "put this on slides," "slide headlines for the [agency] deck," "capability briefing," "make this slide-ready," or hands over raw content and asks for presentation-ready wording. This is the authorized voice standard for BBS federal decks. Always use it so certification discipline (SDVOSB, never DVBE in federal context), federal-traction honesty, and Parker's no-filler, no-em-dash style stay uniform. Do NOT use for CA state agency decks (that context uses DVBE), for email drafts (Parker's email voice lives elsewhere), or for building the .pptx file itself (use the pptx skill for assembly; this skill produces the words).
